author: GamingBolt
description:
Control Resonant is finally getting close to its release, and we managed to sink some serious time into Manhattan, with Dylan being a chaotic vessel for our self-expression on its warped streets.  However, its technical side does deserve some love.

That’s because of how it takes the franchise’s distinct visual identity forward in ways that make it not only look better, but feel better as well. This one’s an evolution, and a good one that makes it an immersive entertainer to join the ranks of this year’s best-looking offerings.
title: Control Resonant Graphics Analysis - Has Remedy Set a New Standard on PS5 Pro and PC?

author: GamingBolt
description:
All in all, Control Resonant is a fantastic game. It builds on the mythos of its predecessor while telling its own emotionally riveting story. I find myself drawn to exploring Manhattan long after the credits roll, unearthing even more paranatural mysteries. 

Even if every "how" and "why" isn't answered, the struggle to maintain control, all for the sake of taking another step forward, remains as endearing as ever.
title: Control Resonant Review - A Genuine Game of the Year Contender

author: GamingBolt
description:
It begins like how many mysteries usually do - with a body. But not just any body - Robert Nightingale, a former FBI agent possessed by Cauldron Lake's paranatural entity. A-010 - The Shadow, or more commonly known as the Dark Presence. Seemingly missing since the events of the first game, he would re-emerge 13 years later - wandering through the woods around Cauldron Lake. 

Not that he got far, as mysterious cult members suddenly accosted and stabbed him. Known as the Cult of the Tree, they've been responsible for a string of murders, prompting a closer look by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Agent Saga Anderson is on the scene alongside Alex Casey.
title: The Full Story of Alan Wake 2 - Before You Play CONTROL Resonant
